experiment.name: phase1_sparsity_mixture
description: Does the cheap-zero step survive a mixture? (critique item E2, the gate for
Phase 3.) Phase 1 measured an all-zero operand against an all-ones one and
found the zero anomalously cheap. Phase 3 wants to read activation sparsity
from power, and real sparse activations are a MIXTURE of zero and non-zero
words. Two mechanisms fit everything measured so far and give opposite
answers:
per-transfer -- each zero word individually saves power. dP falls ~linearly
with the zero fraction, a 50%-sparse tensor inherits half the effect, and
sparsity is recoverable. Phase 3 proceeds.
per-stream -- the cheapness needs sustained zeros (an idle detector, a link
power state, clock gating with hysteresis). dP stays near the full effect
until the buffer is almost all zero, and Phase 3's foundation is gone.
The trap: a scattered mixture is NOT matched on Hamming distance. Randomly
(or evenly) interleaving 0 and 0xFFFFFFFF makes consecutive words differ, and
that switching adds power (Phase 1: +34 mW/flipped bit), peaking at density
0.5 where fillcheck measures 32 flips/transfer ~= +1.1 W of pure switching.
Read naively, the scattered mixture would look expensive and fake a per-stream
answer. So the decisive victim is the BLOCKED one: ws_sparse_l3_x8_blk groups
the zeros into 64-byte runs, holding density and mean Hamming weight identical
but cutting switching ~16x (fillcheck: mean HD 32 -> 2 at d=0.5). Its dP-vs-
density curve answers per-transfer vs per-stream with the switching removed by
construction. The scattered victim is run at the same densities so that
scattered-minus-blocked measures the switching term in-session.
Each run contrasts a density against the all-zero baseline (selector 0), the
same framing as phase1_hamming_weight, so the density-1024 point (all
0xFFFFFFFF) must reproduce that session's hw32 (+1.90 W): it is the built-in
anchor. Selector low 16 bits = nonzero words per 1024; high 32 = pattern (0
ws_iid_l3_x8 (E2b): every bit set independently at the selector's per-1024
probability, so words genuinely differ at a controlled mean bit density. It
tests whether Phase 1's +50.75 mW/bit slope -- measured on ONE repeated word
-- survives non-degenerate data. Note iid has its own switching (mean HD
32*2p(1-p)); it is read as a generalisation check, not a clean weight probe.
Config-A, 3 repeats, shuffled order. warmup_blocks raised because each
distinct density faults and fills a fresh 4 MB slot. The driver also records
the core/uncore split (B1.3), so the mixture effect's domain is available too.
Pre-committed decision rule (blocked victim, dP vs density d = 1-q):
dP(d) ~ d * dP(1), linear through ~origin           -> per-transfer, Phase 3 proceeds
dP(d) ~ dP(1) flat until d small                     -> per-stream, relabel to mean bit density
dP(d) < 0 or non-monotone below the sham floor       -> neither; characterise before proceeding

runs.label: aa_sparse
runs.comment: same density both sides; density-mode measurement path must read zero.

runs.label: blk_d100
runs.comment: blocked, d=1 (all 0xFFFFFFFF): anchor to hw32 +1.90 W.

runs.label: scat_d100
runs.comment: scattered, d=1: must equal blk_d100 (no zeros to place).

runs.label: iid_p50
runs.comment: iid, p=1/2: mean HW 16, words differ.

runs.label: iid_p75
runs.comment: iid, p=3/4: mean HW 24, words differ.
